Driver of Ram 1500 SRT TRX Says He Got People Rolling Their Eyes at Him
14 photos
Photo: ThatDudeinBlue | YouTube
The Ram 1500 SRT TRX is the world's most powerful truck with an internal combustion engine, and you’ve got the HEMI to thank for it. But how is living with such an absurdly powerful vehicle? The man who got to spend a week with it gives an honest review and tells about how he had to help his mother into the cabin and how some roll their eyes when they see him driving the TRX.
Let's do numbers first, because that is where it all begins. The Ram 1500 SRT TRX made a comeback together with the HEMI that former Stellantis CEO Carlos Tavares decided to pull the plug on back in 2023. But with Tavares out of the game and Tim Kuniskis back in , the HEMI returned more powerful than it was when it was discontinued.
So now, Ram’s almighty T-Rex truck comes with the beloved 6.2-liter HEMI V8 with supercharged firepower, now pushing out 777 horsepower (788 metric horsepower) and 680 pound-feet (922 Newton meters) of torque.
That is what makes it rocket from zero to hero (0 to 60 mph or 0 to 97 kph) in 3.5 seconds, flash down the quarter mile in 12.2 seconds with a trap speed of 177 kph, and max out at 118 mph (190 kph), an electronic limit set due to the off-road speed rating of its 35-inch tires. A TorqueFlite 8HP95 8-speed automatic transmission puts the power down through all four corners.
Photo: ThatDudeinBlue | YouTube This is what David Patterson of the ThatDudeinBlue YouTube channel is dealing with since he drove home in the brand-new Ram 1500 SRT TRX for the week of testing. Now, he breaks down the truck's performance, real-world perks and downsides, along with how he feels on board.
Obnoxious, silly, and ridiculous. This is how he describes the truck. First things first: getting into the truck can be a start on the wrong foot because the steps aren't of much help. Olympic gymnast skills would definitely help, but that’s something that David’s mother doesn’t have. So David and his father had to help his mother inside.
The truck, as tested, is a $106,000 deal. That is still cheaper than what Ford is asking for the F-150 Raptor R with the 5.2-liter supercharged V8 under the hood, pumping out less power than Ram’s TRX. The 720-horsepower Ford beast starts at $114,420 before options and taxes. That's the good news.
The bad news is that it gets a brutal 12 miles per gallon average, which translates to 19.6 liters per 100 kilometers. Well, anyone driving it knows well before stepping inside that the Ram 1500 SRT TRX is no Toyota Prius in behavior, stance, or fuel economy. To fill an empty tank, he basically becomes a sponsor of the gas station.
Photo: ThatDudeinBlue | YouTube On full load, the supercharger whines from under the hood, making David call it " the loudest factory supercharger I've ever heard in a modern vehicle ." " It’s a symphony to your ears ," he says. The supercharger, along with the HEMI, makes quite an orchestra that he says he hears better with the windows rolled up.
While driving the truck, David has been getting two very distinct reactions from people who either tell him that he is driving the coolest truck I’ve ever seen in my life or roll their eyes at him, as if they have had enough of men driving full-size high-performance trucks to flatter their ego.
David is well aware that the 1500 SRT TRX is not a truck that requires to be pampered. Besides, he is not the kind of owner who keeps his off-roader on the road. His first experience with the TRX was some high-speed driving in the desert, a show-off jump included in the experience.
That sort of off-road behavior confirmed that the TRX is not all show and no go when it leaves the tarmac behind. He had a similar experience in the Ford F-150 Raptor R in the Saudi Arabian desert, and it “absolutely blew me away.”
{fullimg
But above all, he loves how he rides sky-high in the TRX with high ground clearance and massive 35-inch tires. " I feel I should be holding an American flag out the window with the Blue Angels escorting me ." That is the feeling this high-performance truck gives him while driving.
Given the truck’s $106,000 price tag, owners are right to expect a premium ambiance on board the truck. The TRX that David is testing comes with seats in black leather and contrasting red stitching, along with carbon fiber accents on most touchpoints.
He is content with the 14.5-inch vertical touchscreen, which controls most of the functions of the vehicle. In the meantime, the 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster provides all the relevant driving data. Besides He's got all the driving modes at the tap of a finger.
Accessing the surround-view camera is not that fast, as he has to browse through the menu rather than just hit a button on the dashboard. Furthermore, he says the digital rearview camera can be hit by severe lens glare under direct sunlight. And that rounds up the list of complaints.
